title: Three School distinctions opened: honor per se vs per accidens (king, purple, accidents)
source_text: XXXVI. Ut autem dissensus iste melius percipiatur, ante omnia notandae atque explicandae sunt quaedam distinctiones, quibus uti solent in hac quaestione, ut mentem suam clarius exponant. Primum igitur observant, aliquid honorari vel per se, vel per accidens. Per se, honoratur, inquiunt, suppositum in quo inest ratio venerationis: per accidens, id quod est conjunctum rei quae adoratur, nec est ipsa ratio adorationis. Ut cum honoratur Rex, per se honoratur homo ille, qui est Rex; per accidens honoratur purpura, & reliqua adjuncta, & accidentia omnia ejus, excepta regia dignitate: quae licet non sit id quod honoratur, est tamen id quo homo ille honoratur. Itaque persona honoratur per se, ut quae; regia dignitas honoratur per se, ut qua; reliqua honorantur per accidens.
pass_a_gloss: But so that that disagreement may be better perceived, first of all certain distinctions are to be noted and explained, which they are accustomed to use in this question, so that they may set forth their mind more clearly. First, therefore, they observe that something is honored either per se or per accidents. Per se, they say, the subject is honored in which the reason of veneration is present; per accidents, that which is joined to the thing that is adored and is not itself the reason of adoration. As when a King is honored, per se that man is honored who is King; per accidents the purple is honored, and the remaining adjuncts, and all his accidents, except royal dignity: which, though it is not that which is honored, is nevertheless that by which that man is honored. And so the person is honored per se, as the who; royal dignity is honored per se, as the by-which; the rest are honored per accidents.
pass_b_english: Schoolmen preface the quarrel with distinctions: honor per se vs per accidents.
Per se: the subject that carries the reason of veneration; per accidents: what is merely joined to it.
King example: the man who is king is honored per se; purple and other adjuncts only per accidents—royal dignity is the reason, not an accidental add-on.

choices.why: Scholastic subject of honor, not a mere attribute.
